summary: Duotone's 3-strut Aluula D/TX all-rounder, now with a new 6-point bridle, Micro Batten construction and Micro Loop connections. Runs at up to 10 psi for a very stiff frame; covers freeride, big air, freestyle and wave in one ultralight kite.
best_for: One-kite quivers for riders who want Aluula weight savings across freeride, big air and waves

reviews.summary: Ridden back-to-back with the 2026 Evo D/LAB in 25–28 knots, Kitemana found the 2027 version about half the bar pressure, faster steering, more vertical jumps and more hangtime, and easier to control when overpowered. Loops are easier than before but the 10m flutters late in the loop; the Rebel D/LAB is still the better looper.

structured_review.summary: The 2027 Evo D/LAB brings back the agility the 2026 lost: roughly half the bar pressure, faster steering, more vertical jumps and longer hangtime, and much easier to handle when overpowered. It is a playful all-rounder for intermediate and better riders; the Rebel D/LAB still loops better.
pros: Much lighter bar pressure than the 2026 model
More vertical jumps and longer hangtime with an easier downloop
Easier to control when overpowered or gusty
Versatile across freeride, foil, wave and freestyle
cons: Loop slows and flutters late on the 10m
The Rebel D/LAB is still the better kiteloop kite
Less forgiving than the standard Evo; not for beginners
structured_review.best_for: Intermediate and advanced all-round riders who want one Aluula kite for big air, freeride, foil and waves.
structured_review.not_for: Beginners, or riders whose only focus is kiteloops.
structured_review.rec_blurb: Half the bar pressure, more hangtime: the Evo D/LAB gets playful again.
